label: EU digital and cyber resilience
summary: EU laws that apply by entity type and size, not by choice: DORA for financial entities and NIS2 for essential and important entities in listed sectors. The authority first asks which regime and class the entity falls under, in which member state it is registered, who in the management body is accountable, what the register or supplier list looks like, and how the incident reporting clocks will be met.

source.ref: DORA Art. 2 (financial entities in scope), Art. 16 (simplified framework) and Art. 26 (threat-led testing); NIS2 Arts 2 and 3 (sectors, size rule, essential and important entities), Art. 26 (jurisdiction) and Art. 27 (registry)

fields.label: Entities
fields.note: Legal entities the regime applies to, picked from the organisation profile. Both regimes apply to the individual legal entity, so a group lists each member in scope.

fields.label: Entity type
fields.note: DORA Art. 2 lists the financial entities in scope, from banks and insurers to crypto-asset providers and pension funds. The type decides the competent authority and whether a simplified regime can apply. Pick the closest.

fields.label: Competent authority

source.ref: EBA DORA pages: registers of information and major incident reports are submitted to the national competent authority

fields.note: National authority that supervises the entity under DORA. It receives the register of information and major incident reports, and it sets the entity's own deadlines.

fields.label: Size class
fields.note: Art. 16 gives a simplified framework only to the small categories it names, not to any small firm. Microenterprises stay on the full framework with some relief (for example Art. 5(3)). Confirm the class with the authority.

fields.label: LEI

source.ref: EBA FAQ on reporting the registers of information (28 March 2025): files are named and submitted under the reporting entity's LEI

fields.note: Legal entity identifier of the financial entity. The register of information is reported under the entity's LEI, and authorities identify the entity by it.

fields.label: TLPT status
fields.note: Art. 26: entities the authority designates carry out threat-led penetration testing, normally every three years. Record whether the entity has been told. The selection criteria are the authority's, not the entity's.

fields.label: Sector

source.ref: Commission NIS2 page and FAQ: 18 critical sectors in Annexes I and II; medium and large entities in them are in scope

fields.note: NIS2 covers 18 critical sectors in Annexes I and II. Medium and large entities in them are in scope, and some entity types are in scope whatever their size (Art. 2). Pick the closest and check the national law.

fields.label: Sub-sector
fields.note: Sub-sector or entity type as named in the annex. Registration data and the competent authority depend on it.

fields.label: Staff
fields.note: Headcount for the size rule, prefilled from the organisation profile. Confirm the figure that counts for this entity.

fields.label: Annual turnover
fields.note: Annual turnover for the size rule, prefilled from the organisation profile, in the profile currency.

fields.label: Size class

source.ref: Commission NIS2 FAQ: size threshold rule; Member States may add smaller entities with a high risk profile

fields.note: NIS2 applies a size threshold: medium and large entities in the listed sectors are in scope, and Member States may add smaller high-risk ones (Commission FAQ). Pick the class that applies to this entity.

fields.label: Entity class

source.ref: Commission NIS2 FAQ: essential and important entities, supervision regime and minimum fine ceilings

fields.note: Essential or important decides the supervision regime and the fine ceiling (at least EUR 10m or 2% for essential, EUR 7m or 1.4% for important). Each Member State confirms the class under its own law.

fields.label: Member states

source.ref: National transposition laws (not individually checked); Commission transposition page

fields.note: One row per EU country where the entity is established or serves. Each has its own law, authority and register, so class and registration are recorded per country. National laws were not individually checked (unverified).

fields.label: Main establishment

source.ref: Commission NIS2 FAQ and Art. 26: listed digital entities fall under the country of their main EU establishment

fields.note: DNS, TLD, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed service and security providers, marketplaces, search engines and social networks fall under the country of their main EU establishment (Art. 26). Others follow where they are established.

fields.label: Outside the EU

source.ref: Commission NIS2 FAQ and Art. 26: entities not established in the Union designate a representative

fields.note: Tick when the entity is not established in the EU but offers services there.

fields.label: EU representative

source.ref: Commission NIS2 FAQ and Art. 26: entities not established in the Union designate a representative

fields.note: Listed entity types not established in the EU must designate a representative in a country where they offer services (Art. 26), and the authority records where it is. Enter the representative.

source.ref: DORA Art. 5 (the management body defines, approves and oversees; budget; third-party policy; training) and NIS2 Art. 20 (management bodies approve and oversee the risk-management measures and follow training) with Art. 21

fields.label: ICT strategy
fields.note: Art. 5(2): the management body sets and approves the digital operational resilience strategy, including ICT risk tolerance. Record where it stands; any status is accepted at onboarding.

fields.label: Third-party policy
fields.note: Art. 5(2): the management body approves and reviews the policy on using ICT services from third-party providers. Record where it stands.

fields.label: ICT budget
fields.note: Art. 5(2): the management body allocates and reviews the budget for digital operational resilience, including ICT security awareness and training.

fields.label: ICT risk owner
fields.note: Person or function accountable to the management body for managing and overseeing ICT risk (Art. 5).

fields.label: Third-party monitor
fields.note: Art. 5(3): entities other than microenterprises set up a role to monitor ICT third-party arrangements, or designate a senior manager responsible for overseeing the risk exposure and documentation.

fields.label: Testing programme
fields.note: Status of the digital operational resilience testing programme (Arts 24 and 25).

fields.label: Approver
fields.note: NIS2 Art. 20(1): the management body approves the cybersecurity risk-management measures, oversees them and can be held liable. Name the person who signs for it.

fields.label: Risk policies
fields.note: Status of the risk analysis and information security policies NIS2 lists first among its measures (Art. 21).

fields.label: Measures approved
fields.note: Date the management body approved the risk-management measures (Art. 20(1), Art. 21). Leave empty if not yet approved.

fields.label: Management training
fields.note: Latest ICT or cyber training for the management body. DORA Art. 5(4) and NIS2 Art. 20(2) both require members to follow training on a regular basis.

source.ref: DORA register of information: ITS on the templates and the EBA preparation page and FAQ (28 March 2025): entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated registers, plain CSV, collected by the competent authority for the ESAs

fields.label: Register status
fields.note: DORA requires a register of all contractual arrangements with ICT third-party providers, kept at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level. The authority collects it each year for the ESAs.

fields.label: Register levels
fields.note: The register must be available at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level (EBA). Pick the levels that apply to this group structure.

fields.label: ICT providers
fields.note: ICT third-party providers the entity has arrangements with, picked from the organisation profile. Every one belongs in the register, not only the critical ones.

fields.label: Provider LEIs
fields.note: Providers are identified in the register by legal entity identifier where they have one. Collect them early; chasing providers at submission time is slow.

fields.label: Contract clauses
fields.note: Whether the key contractual provisions DORA lists (Art. 30) are in the ICT contracts.

fields.label: Critical functions
fields.note: Business functions the entity treats as critical or important, with the provider that supports each. The register flags the arrangements that support them.

fields.label: CTPP list checked

source.ref: EBA DORA oversight page: the ESAs designate critical ICT third-party providers and publish the list; first list published 18 November 2025

fields.note: The ESAs publish the list of critical ICT third-party providers (first list: 18 November 2025). Check which of the entity's providers are on it.

fields.label: Next submission
fields.note: The authority sets the entity's deadline, earlier than its own 31 March report to the ESAs (reference date 31 December). Ask the authority for the date.

source.ref: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) and 21(3): supply chain security, direct suppliers' vulnerabilities and cybersecurity practices

fields.label: Suppliers
fields.note: Direct suppliers and service providers that affect the entity's network and information systems, picked from the organisation profile. Art. 21(2)(d) puts supply chain security in the minimum measures.

fields.label: Supplier policy
fields.note: A policy on supplier security: requirements in contracts, assessment and monitoring. Art. 21(2)(d) names the relationship with direct suppliers.

fields.label: Suppliers assessed
fields.note: Art. 21(3): when choosing measures, entities take account of the vulnerabilities specific to each direct supplier and the quality of its products and cybersecurity practices, including secure development.

source.ref: DORA major incident reporting standards (EBA): initial notice 4 h after classification and 24 h after detection, intermediate 72 h, final in one month; NIS2 Art. 23 and Commission FAQ: early warning 24 h, notification 72 h, final report within a month

fields.label: Classification process
fields.note: A written way to decide which incidents are reportable: DORA classifies major ICT-related incidents by set criteria, NIS2 asks for notice of significant incidents. Without it the clocks cannot be met.

fields.label: Reporting clocks
fields.note: DORA: initial notice within 4 h of classifying a major incident and at most 24 h after becoming aware, intermediate 72 h after the initial notice, final one month after the last intermediate report. NIS2: early warning 24 h, notification 72 h, final report in one month.

fields.label: Reporting contact
fields.note: Person who files incident reports with the authority and is reachable inside the clocks.

fields.label: Authority channel
fields.note: Portal, address or CSIRT the reports go to. DORA reports go to the competent authority; NIS2 early warnings go to the CSIRT or competent authority.

gate.label: The DORA entity type is decided
gate.hint: Check Art. 2 and pick the entity type, or record that the entity is not an Article 2 entity.

gate.label: The ICT risk owner is named
gate.hint: Name who answers to the management body for ICT risk.

gate.label: The register of information is started
gate.hint: The register is due every year; start by listing providers and contracts.

gate.label: The TLPT status is known
gate.hint: Ask the authority whether the entity is designated for threat-led testing.

gate.label: The NIS2 entity class is decided
gate.hint: Decide essential, important or not in scope from the sector and size.

gate.label: Essential entities are registered or have a date set
gate.hint: Register with the national authority, or set the date, in each country where the entity is essential.

gate.label: Important entities are registered or have a date set
gate.hint: Register with the national authority, or set the date, in each country where the entity is important.

gate.label: The management body approver is named
gate.hint: Name who approves the risk-management measures for the management body.

gate.label: Management training is dated
gate.hint: Both regimes expect the management body to follow training; record the latest date.

gate.label: An incident classification process exists
gate.hint: The 4-hour and 24-hour clocks leave no time to design a process during an incident.

gate.label: A planned registration has a date
gate.hint: Enter the date registration is planned for.
